method: yEnc shifts every payload byte by 42 modulo 256, so byte b becomes the character (b + 42) mod 256. When that character would be NUL, LF, CR or '=', or a tab or space at the start of a line, it is written as '=' followed by (character + 64) mod 256; a decoder recovers the byte as (escaped character - 106) mod 256. Line breaks inside the body are framing and are removed before decoding. The encoder wraps at the chosen line length without splitting an escape pair and, when headers are enabled, writes =ybegin line=N size=N name=file, the body, and =yend size=N crc32=XXXXXXXX. The checksum is the reflected IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 (polynomial 0xEDB88320, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF) over the original bytes, shown as eight lowercase hex digits. Typed text is encoded as its UTF-8 bytes. The decoder accepts CRLF or LF, ignores article headers above =ybegin and any =ypart markers, verifies the =yend size and CRC32 when present, and reports a mismatch as a warning instead of hiding it. A payload that is not valid UTF-8 is shown as hex. Encoding is capped at 100,000 characters and decoding at 200,000 characters, and everything runs in the browser with no uploads, network access or storage.

sources.title: yEnc encodes each byte as (byte + 42) mod 256 and escapes NUL, LF, CR, '=' and a leading tab or space as '=' plus (character + 64) mod 256.
The =ybegin, =ypart and =yend lines carry the line length, part and total size, file name and a CRC32 checksum; body line breaks are framing, not data.
CRC-32 as used by zip and PNG is the reflected IEEE 802.3 polynomial 0xEDB88320 with an initial value of 0xFFFFFFFF and a final XOR of 0xFFFFFFFF.
